claim: Zebra finches are sexually dimorphic vocal learners.
source: Zebra finches are sexually dimorphic vocal learners.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract that establishes the basic characteristic of the study organism.

claim: Male zebra finches learn to sing by imitating mature conspecifics, but females do not.
source: Males learn to sing by imitating mature conspecifics, but females do not.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing the sexually dimorphic vocal learning behavior.

claim: Absence of song in females is associated with partial atrophy and apparent repression of several vocal learning brain regions during development.
source: Absence of song in females is associated with partial atrophy and apparent repression of several vocal learning brain regions during development.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing anatomical differences associated with the lack of vocal learning in females.

claim: Atrophy can be prevented, and vocal learning retained in females when given early pharmacological estrogen treatment.
source: However, atrophy can be prevented, and vocal learning retained in females when given early pharmacological estrogen treatment.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing the effect of estrogen treatment on female zebra finches.

claim: Female HVC and Area X gene modules were specialized by estrogen supplementation, exhibiting a subset of the transcriptomic specializations observed in males.
source: Female HVC and Area X gene modules were specialized by estrogen supplementation, exhibiting a subset of the transcriptomic specializations observed in males.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract summarizing a key finding from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Female robust nucleus of the arcopallium (RA) and lateral magnocellular nucleus of the anterior nidopallium (LMAN) specialized modules were less dependent on estrogen.
source: Female robust nucleus of the arcopallium (RA) and lateral magnocellular nucleus of the anterior nidopallium (LMAN) specialized modules were less dependent on estrogen.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract summarizing a key finding about regional differences in estrogen dependence.

claim: The estrogen-induced gene modules in females were enriched for anatomical development functions.
source: The estrogen-induced gene modules in females were enriched for anatomical development functions and strongly correlated to the expression of several Z sex chromosome genes.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing functional enrichment analysis results.

claim: The estrogen-induced gene modules in females were strongly correlated to the expression of several Z sex chromosome genes.
source: The estrogen-induced gene modules in females were enriched for anatomical development functions and strongly correlated to the expression of several Z sex chromosome genes.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing a key finding about the relationship between estrogen-induced modules and Z chromosome genes.

claim: Reduced dosage and expression of Z chromosome genes suppress the full development of the song system and thus song learning behavior.
source: We present a hypothesis where reduced dosage and expression of these Z chromosome genes suppress the full development of the song system and thus song learning behavior, which is partially rescued by estrogen treatment.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract presenting the authors' hypothesis based on their findings.

claim: Estrogen treatment partially rescues the suppression of song system development caused by reduced Z chromosome gene dosage.
source: We present a hypothesis where reduced dosage and expression of these Z chromosome genes suppress the full development of the song system and thus song learning behavior, which is partially rescued by estrogen treatment.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract presenting the authors' hypothesis about the mechanism of estrogen rescue.

claim: Vocal learning is found in seven nonhuman clades, four mammalian and three avian.
source: Vocal learning is found in seven nonhuman clades, four mammalian and three avian, each having independently evolved the trait (Jarvis, 2019; Jarvis et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Each vocal learning clade has independently evolved the trait.
source: Vocal learning is found in seven nonhuman clades, four mammalian and three avian, each having independently evolved the trait (Jarvis, 2019; Jarvis et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: There is remarkable evolutionary convergence between songbird and human vocal learning in terms of behavioral progression.
source: Despite ~300 million years of separation from their common ancestor (Kumar and Hedges, 1998; van Tuinen and Hadly, 2004), there is remarkable evolutionary convergence between songbird and human vocal learning in terms of behavioral progression, developmental effects of deafening, anatomical connectivity of vocal-motor learning circuits, sites of accelerated evolution within the genome, and genes with specialized up- or downregulated expression in song and speech circuits relative to the surrounding motor control circuits (Jarvis, 2019; Bolhuis et al., 2010; Doupe and Kuhl, 1999; Mooney, 2009; Pfenning et al., 2014; Feenders et al., 2008; Gedman et al., 2022; Cahill et al., 2021; Li et al., 2007; Lovell et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Songbirds and humans have been separated from their common ancestor for approximately 300 million years.
source: Despite ~300 million years of separation from their common ancestor (Kumar and Hedges, 1998; van Tuinen and Hadly, 2004), there is remarkable evolutionary convergence between songbird and human vocal learning in terms of behavioral progression, developmental effects of deafening, anatomical connectivity of vocal-motor learning circuits, sites of accelerated evolution within the genome, and genes with specialized up- or downregulated expression in song and speech circuits relative to the surrounding motor control circuits (Jarvis, 2019; Bolhuis et al., 2010; Doupe and Kuhl, 1999; Mooney, 2009; Pfenning et al., 2014; Feenders et al., 2008; Gedman et al., 2022; Cahill et al., 2021; Li et al., 2007; Lovell et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Vocal learning is strongly sexually dimorphic in zebra finches and many other vocal learning species.
source: Unlike in humans, however, vocal learning is strongly sexually dimorphic in zebra finches and many other vocal learning species (Nottebohm and Arnold, 1976; Odom et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Male zebra finches learn to produce a species-appropriate song by imitating mature male conspecifics during juvenile development.
source: Male zebra finches learn to produce a species-appropriate song by imitating mature male conspecifics during juvenile development, while females are limited to producing innate calls (Zann, 1997).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Female zebra finches are limited to producing innate calls.
source: Male zebra finches learn to produce a species-appropriate song by imitating mature male conspecifics during juvenile development, while females are limited to producing innate calls (Zann, 1997).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The songbird vocal motor learning circuit contains four major interconnected telencephalic song control nuclei: HVC, LMAN, RA, and Area X.
source: The songbird vocal motor learning circuit contains four major interconnected telencephalic song control nuclei: HVC (proper name) in the dorsal nidopallium (DN); the lateral magnocellular nucleus of the anterior nidopallium (LMAN) in the anterior nidopallium (AN); the robust nucleus of the arcopallium (RA) in the lateral intermediate arcopallium (LAI; also called AId); and Area X in the striatum (Str; Figure 1a; Mooney, 2009).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with a supporting citation and reference to Figure 1a.

claim: During juvenile development in zebra finch females, HVC and RA atrophy.
source: During juvenile development in zebra finch females, HVC and RA atrophy, HVC fails to form synapses in RA, and Area X never appears (Nottebohm and Arnold, 1976; Bottjer et al., 1985; Garcia Calero and Scharff, 2013; Konishi and Akutagawa, 1985; Nixdorf-Bergweiler, 1996; Nordeen and Nordeen, 1988; Shaughnessy et al., 2019; Holloway and Clayton, 2001; Mooney and Rao, 1994).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: During juvenile development in zebra finch females, HVC fails to form synapses in RA.
source: During juvenile development in zebra finch females, HVC and RA atrophy, HVC fails to form synapses in RA, and Area X never appears (Nottebohm and Arnold, 1976; Bottjer et al., 1985; Garcia Calero and Scharff, 2013; Konishi and Akutagawa, 1985; Nixdorf-Bergweiler, 1996; Nordeen and Nordeen, 1988; Shaughnessy et al., 2019; Holloway and Clayton, 2001; Mooney and Rao, 1994).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: During juvenile development in zebra finch females, Area X never appears.
source: During juvenile development in zebra finch females, HVC and RA atrophy, HVC fails to form synapses in RA, and Area X never appears (Nottebohm and Arnold, 1976; Bottjer et al., 1985; Garcia Calero and Scharff, 2013; Konishi and Akutagawa, 1985; Nixdorf-Bergweiler, 1996; Nordeen and Nordeen, 1988; Shaughnessy et al., 2019; Holloway and Clayton, 2001; Mooney and Rao, 1994).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Female zebra finches treated with estrogen or a synthetic analog at an early age do not exhibit song system atrophy.
source: Amazingly, female zebra finches treated with estrogen or a synthetic analog at an early age do not exhibit song system atrophy and instead form a functional neural circuit with all the anatomical components and connections seen in males (Gurney and Konishi, 1980; Gurney, 1982; Simpson and Vicario, 1991a; Simpson and Vicario, 1991b).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Female zebra finches treated with estrogen at an early age form a functional neural circuit with all the anatomical components and connections seen in males.
source: Amazingly, female zebra finches treated with estrogen or a synthetic analog at an early age do not exhibit song system atrophy and instead form a functional neural circuit with all the anatomical components and connections seen in males (Gurney and Konishi, 1980; Gurney, 1982; Simpson and Vicario, 1991a; Simpson and Vicario, 1991b).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The 'masculinized' song system allows estrogen-supplemented females to imitate vocalizations, though not with the same accuracy as males.
source: This 'masculinized' song system allows estrogen-supplemented females to imitate vocalizations, though not with the same accuracy as males (Gurney and Konishi, 1980; Simpson and Vicario, 1991a; Choe et al., 2021; Pohl Apel, 1985; Pohl Apel and Sossinka, 1984).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Lesioning female HVC prevents estrogen-dependent anatomical 'masculinization' of its postsynaptic targets to RA and Area X.
source: Interestingly, lesioning female HVC prevents estrogen-dependent anatomical 'masculinization' of its postsynaptic targets to RA and Area X (Herrmann and Arnold, 1991).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: A rare gynandromorphic zebra finch with lateralized sex chromosome composition indicates that genetically male HVC and Area X are larger than their female analogs independent of gonadal hormone production.
source: However, the examination of a rare gynandromorphic zebra finch with lateralized sex chromosome composition indicates that genetically male HVC and Area X are larger than their female analogs independent of gonadal hormone production, implicating sex chromosome gene expression within the song system (Agate et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Birds have a Z and W sex determination system where females are hemizygous (ZW) and males homozygous (ZZ).
source: Unlike the mammalian X and Y, birds have a Z and W sex determination system where females are hemizygous (ZW) and males homozygous (ZZ) (Gianaroli et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The relevant transcriptional machinery for song system development appears to be set up by post-hatch day 30 (PHD30).
source: The relevant transcriptional machinery appears to be set up by post-hatch day 30 (PHD30), after which estrogen fails to masculinize female song nuclei or behavior, and the male song system enlarges while the female song system atrophies (Bottjer et al., 1985; Konishi and Akutagawa, 1985; Gurney and Konishi, 1980; Konishi and Akutagawa, 1988).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: After PHD30, estrogen fails to masculinize female song nuclei or behavior.
source: The relevant transcriptional machinery appears to be set up by post-hatch day 30 (PHD30), after which estrogen fails to masculinize female song nuclei or behavior, and the male song system enlarges while the female song system atrophies (Bottjer et al., 1985; Konishi and Akutagawa, 1985; Gurney and Konishi, 1980; Konishi and Akutagawa, 1988).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Vocal learning in females was lost multiple independent times among songbirds.
source: Taken together with the hypothesis that vocal learning in females was lost multiple independent times among songbirds (Odom et al., 2014), the extant findings suggest genetic drivers of vocal learning loss associated with estrogen, sex chromosomes, and song nuclei gene expression specializations.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Female finches treated with E2 in the same way as in this study go on to produce rudimentary imitative songs as adults.
source: While the birds for this study were sacrificed prior to the developmental presentation of song behavior, we have previously shown that female finches treated with E2 in the same exact way go on to produce rudimentary imitative songs as adults, consistent with the known induction of vocal learning in females by E2 (Gurney and Konishi, 1980; Choe et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: 13,220 genes were well expressed in the finch telencephalic brain regions sampled.
source: Of the ~21,000 annotated zebra finch genes, 13,220 were well expressed in the finch telencephalic brain regions sampled, a comparable number of genes to what we have seen expressed in adult zebra finch telencephalon (Gedman et al., 2021; Gedman, 2021).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section describing the number of expressed genes identified.

claim: 13,220 genes were assigned to 14 co-expression modules.
source: These 13,220 were assigned to 14 co-expression modules (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: The median observation of unassigned transcripts was 22-fold lower than the median observation of module-assigned transcripts.
source: The median observation of unassigned transcripts was 22-fold lower than the median observation of module-assigned transcripts (4.86 vs 0.22 FPKM).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section describing the expression levels of unassigned vs assigned transcripts.

claim: Two modules clearly marked single samples from two different birds, indicative of technical overfitting.
source: Two modules clearly marked single samples from two different birds (Figure 1—figure supplement 4a and b - arrows), indicative of technical overfitting; these two modules (not birds) were excluded from further analysis, resulting in a more visibly diverse pattern within and across modules (Figure 1—figure supplement 4c, d).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: The remaining 12 modules contained 12,444 genes in total.
source: The remaining 12 modules contained 12,444 genes in total; these 12 modules were lettered in descending order of size A through L, containing from 4890 to 127 constituent genes each, which were dynamically expressed across brain regions and treatment groups (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Each song nucleus in vehicle-treated control males had unique and overlapping specialization of genes in 2–4 modules of the 12.
source: Each song nucleus in vehicle-treated control males had unique and overlapping specialization of genes in 2–4 modules of the 12 (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Area X was the only song nucleus that did not have a specialized module unique to it relative to other song nuclei.
source: Area X was the only song nucleus that did not have a specialized module unique to it relative to other song nuclei (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: In nonvocal learning juvenile females, LMAN was specialized relative to AN by the same gene modules as in males (B, F, and I) as well as an additional module G.
source: In nonvocal learning juvenile females, interestingly, LMAN was specialized relative to AN by the same gene modules as in males (B, F, and I) as well as an additional module G (Figure 2b); RA was specialized by module A as in males, but not module L and by additional modules A and G.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: In nonvocal learning juvenile females, RA was specialized by module A as in males, but not module L and by additional modules A and G.
source: In nonvocal learning juvenile females, interestingly, LMAN was specialized relative to AN by the same gene modules as in males (B, F, and I) as well as an additional module G (Figure 2b); RA was specialized by module A as in males, but not module L and by additional modules A and G.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Neither juvenile female HVC nor Area X exhibited significant gene module expression specializations relative to their surrounds.
source: In contrast, neither juvenile female HVC nor Area X exhibited significant gene module expression specializations relative to their surrounds.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section describing the lack of specialization in female HVC and Area X.

claim: In E2-treated juvenile males, the song nuclei-specialized modules overlapped with those seen in vehicle-treated males.
source: In the E2-treated juvenile males, the song nuclei-specialized modules overlapped with those seen in vehicle-treated males (Figure 2a vs c).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: E2-treated females more closely mirrored the gene module specializations seen in the vehicle-treated male song system.
source: In contrast, E2-treated females more closely mirrored the gene module specializations seen in the vehicle-treated male song system (Figure 2a vs d).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: The transcriptional response of female song nuclei to E2 treatment appeared to be far more dramatic than in males.
source: That is, the transcriptional response of female song nuclei to E2 treatment appeared to be far more dramatic than in males.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section summarizing the sex-specific effects of E2 treatment.

claim: Module F in LMAN, module G in HVC, module C in RA, and modules C, F, and G in Area X are four core modules for song nuclei that are the most sensitive to E2 induction or enhancement in females and most associated with the presence of vocal learning in females.
source: These were: module F in LMAN; module G in HVC; module C in RA; and modules C, F, and G in Area X. That is, these are four core modules for song nuclei that are the most sensitive to E2 induction or enhancement in females and most associated with the presence of vocal learning in females.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section identifying key modules associated with vocal learning.

claim: Module E strongly correlated with higher expression in all male brain regions relative to females.
source: We compared vehicle-treated male and female song nuclei and surrounds separately and found that module E strongly correlated with higher expression in all male brain regions relative to females (Figure 2f, g).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: Module G eigengene expression was significantly higher in male HVC and Area X.
source: Among the song nuclei, module G eigengene expression was significantly higher in male HVC and Area X; conversely, module C expression was higher in female LMAN and RA (Figure 2f).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Module C expression was higher in female LMAN and RA.
source: Among the song nuclei, module G eigengene expression was significantly higher in male HVC and Area X; conversely, module C expression was higher in female LMAN and RA (Figure 2f).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Module H eigengene expression was significantly higher in female DN.
source: Among the surrounds, module H eigengene expression (not significant in any other comparison) was significantly higher in female DN, and module C was significantly higher in female AN and Str (Figure 2g).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Module C was significantly higher in female AN and Str.
source: Among the surrounds, module H eigengene expression (not significant in any other comparison) was significantly higher in female DN, and module C was significantly higher in female AN and Str (Figure 2g).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Module A was highly expressed in all Area X and Str samples, regardless of treatment or sex.
source: Module A, which appeared specialized in RA relative to LAI in several comparisons, was highly expressed in all Area X and Str samples, regardless of treatment or sex (Figure 2h).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: FOXP2 was a potent member of module A, correlating with the eigengene at r2=0.92 across all samples.
source: Interestingly, FOXP2, a gene critical for spoken-language and vocal learning in humans (Lai et al., 2001) and songbirds (Teramitsu and White, 2006), was a potent member of module A, correlating with the eigengene at r2=0.92 across all samples.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: Module C was most highly expressed in arcopallial samples, especially RA, with some increase in HVC.
source: Module C, which was specialized to RA, HVC, and Area X relative to their surrounds and sexually dimorphic in LMAN and Str, was most highly expressed in arcopallial samples, especially RA, with some increase in HVC (Figure 2i).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Module F was highly expressed exclusively in LMAN regardless of sex and E2 treatment.
source: Module F, which was specialized to LMAN relative to its surround in all such comparisons, was highly expressed exclusively in LMAN regardless of sex and E2 treatment (Figure 2j).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Module G was only highly expressed in HVC samples, with males having higher expression than females, and females further split by treatment.
source: Module G, which was specialized to HVC in a sex- and E2-dependent manner, was only highly expressed in HVC samples, with males having higher expression than females, and females further split by treatment (Figure 2k).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Module J was highly expressed in all samples of animal 'b', an E2-treated female.
source: At the other extreme, three small modules showed higher expression specific to individual birds: module J was highly expressed in all samples of animal 'b', an E2-treated female (Figure 2m); module K was highly expressed across all samples of animal 'f' vehicle-treated female, and at roughly half-dose in animal 'g', an E2-treated male (Figure 2n); module L was highly expressed in animal 'a', another E2-treated female (Figure 2o).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Module K was highly expressed across all samples of animal 'f' vehicle-treated female, and at roughly half-dose in animal 'g', an E2-treated male.
source: At the other extreme, three small modules showed higher expression specific to individual birds: module J was highly expressed in all samples of animal 'b', an E2-treated female (Figure 2m); module K was highly expressed across all samples of animal 'f' vehicle-treated female, and at roughly half-dose in animal 'g', an E2-treated male (Figure 2n); module L was highly expressed in animal 'a', another E2-treated female (Figure 2o).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Module L was highly expressed in animal 'a', another E2-treated female.
source: At the other extreme, three small modules showed higher expression specific to individual birds: module J was highly expressed in all samples of animal 'b', an E2-treated female (Figure 2m); module K was highly expressed across all samples of animal 'f' vehicle-treated female, and at roughly half-dose in animal 'g', an E2-treated male (Figure 2n); module L was highly expressed in animal 'a', another E2-treated female (Figure 2o).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Of the 12,444 module-assigned genes, 7909 (63%) had 1:1 human orthologs annotated in Ensembl.
source: Of the 12,444 module-assigned genes, 7909 (63%) had 1:1 human orthologs annotated in Ensembl.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section describing the mapping of zebra finch genes to human orthologs.

claim: Module G genes specialized in male and E2-treated female HVC and Area X potentially act to integrate and differentiate late-born neurons.
source: We found GO terms significantly enriched in module G, which included 'DNA binding transcription factor activity', 'cell differentiation', 'anatomical morphogenesis', 'cell-to-cell signaling', and 'positive regulation of multicellular organism growth', indicating that module G genes specialized in male and E2-treated female HVC and Area X potentially act to integrate and differentiate late-born neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section describing GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: Module G may act to restructure the extracellular matrix, perhaps to accommodate new cells.
source: Other significantly enriched terms were 'extracellular matrix structural component', 'external side of the plasma membrane', and 'extracellular space', indicating that this module may also act to restructure the extracellular matrix, perhaps to accommodate new cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section describing GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: Module E had six significantly enriched GO terms, of which three pertained to DNA damage repair: 'nucleolus', 'transcription, DNA templated', and 'U2-type precatalytic spliceosome'.
source: Module E, which was differential between the sexes for both song nuclei and surrounds, had six significantly enriched terms, of which three pertained to DNA damage repair: 'nucleolus', 'transcription, DNA templated', and 'U2-type precatalytic spliceosome'.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section describing GO enrichment analysis results.

claim: There is a sexually dimorphic gene expression program broadly distributed across the finch telencephalon that likely acts within the nuclear environment.
source: These results in module E indicate that there is a sexually dimorphic gene expression program broadly distributed across the finch telencephalon that likely acts within the nuclear environment.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section interpreting GO enrichment results.

claim: Module B, specialized to both LMAN and HVC, was enriched for the convergently specialized genes in human dLMC known to match the upper layers of the cortex.
source: We found that module B, specialized to both LMAN and HVC (Figure 2a), was enriched for the convergently specialized genes in human dLMC (Figure 3a) known to match the upper layers of the cortex (Feenders et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to figures and a citation.

claim: Module C, specialized to RA, was enriched for the genes convergently specialized in dLMC and RA known to match the lower layers of the cortex.
source: Module C, specialized to RA (Figure 2a , i), was enriched for the genes convergently specialized in dLMC and RA (Figure 3a) known to match the lower layers of the cortex (Feenders et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to figures and a citation.

claim: Module A, highly expressed in Area X and Str, was enriched for genes convergently specialized in Area X and human anterior striatum (both caudate and putamen).
source: Module A, highly expressed in Area X and Str (Figure 2h), was enriched for genes convergently specialized in Area X and human anterior striatum (both caudate and putamen; Figure 3a).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: Module I, specialized to Area X, was even more strongly enriched for the same convergences as module A.
source: Module I, specialized to Area X (Figure 2a), was also even more strongly enriched for the same convergences as module A (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to figures.

claim: Each of the 12 modules was enriched for genes from at least one chromosome.
source: Surprisingly, we found that each of the 12 modules was enriched for genes from at least one chromosome (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Module E genes were enriched on the Z and W sex chromosomes, with nearly all W expressed genes and ~⅔ of Z expressed genes being members of module E.
source: The most striking was module E genes, which were enriched on the Z and W sex chromosomes, with nearly all W expressed genes and ~⅔ of Z expressed genes being members of module E.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section describing chromosome enrichment results.

claim: Two HVC specialized gene modules (B and G) were significantly enriched on chromosome 1A.
source: For the autosomes, we observed significant enrichments of two HVC specialized gene modules on chromosome 1A: module B (specialized in male HVC and human dLMC) and module G (specialized in male HVC and E2-treated female HVC and sexually dimorphic in vehicle-treated HVC).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section describing chromosome enrichment results.

claim: Zebra finch chromosomes 1 and 1A are believed to be the result of a songbird-specific fragmentation of the ancestral chromosome 1 found in chickens.
source: These results are particularly interesting given that zebra finch chromosomes 1 and 1A are believed to be the result of a songbird-specific fragmentation of the ancestral chromosome 1 found in chickens (Itoh and Arnold, 2005; Warren et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: Module A was enriched across five macrochromosomes (chr1, 2, 3, 4, and 10).
source: Module A, the largest module, which was highly expressed in Area X and adjacent striatum, was enriched across five macrochromosomes (chr1, 2, 3, 4, and 10).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section describing chromosome enrichment results.

claim: Module F, which was strongly expressed in LMAN, was enriched on chromosomes 2 and 7.
source: Module F, which was strongly expressed in LMAN, was enriched on chromosomes 2 and 7.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section describing chromosome enrichment results.

claim: Modules C and I were enriched on chromosome 6 and microchromosome 35.
source: Modules C (most strongly expressed in the arcopallium and part of RA and Area X specializations) and I (a component of the LMAN specialization) were enriched on chromosome 6 and microchromosome 35.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section describing chromosome enrichment results.

claim: Module D was enriched across eight small microchromosomes (chr22, 23, 25, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31).
source: Module D, a component of the LMAN specialization in E2-treated females, was enriched across eight small microchromosomes (chr22, 23, 25, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section describing chromosome enrichment results.

claim: Z transcripts were positively correlated to the MEG-E while W transcripts were anticorrelated.
source: Doing this for module E, we found that Z transcripts were positively correlated to the MEG while W transcripts were anticorrelated (Figure 4e).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: The general reduction in female Z chromosome transcript abundance within module E is consistent with the finding that diploid Z chromosomes in male birds do not have one copy inactivated to compensate for gene dosage.
source: This general reduction in female Z chromosome transcript abundance within module E is consistent with the finding that diploid Z chromosomes in male birds do not have one copy inactivated to compensate for gene dosage, unlike the X inactivation in female mammals (Agate et al., 2003; Itoh et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: A total of 95 W and 694 Z chromosome genes were differentially expressed between sexes in at least one brain region, 62% and 65% of annotated sex chromosome genes, respectively.
source: Examining the union of these gene sets revealed that a total of 95 W and 694 Z chromosome genes were differentially expressed between sexes in at least one brain region, 62% and 65% of annotated sex chromosome genes, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section describing sex chromosome expression analysis.

claim: 58 significantly expressed W chromosome genes and 306 significantly depleted Z chromosome genes were found in all nonvocal regions in females, representing 38% and 29% of annotated sex chromosome genes, respectively.
source: Conversely, the intersection of these regional gene sets contained 58 significantly expressed W chromosome genes and 306 significantly depleted Z chromosome genes in all nonvocal regions in females, representing 38% and 29% of annotated sex chromosome genes, respectively (Figure 4h, i, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the Results section with reference to a figure and supplementary file.
